title: Stride-aware l2norm_fwd (2D grid over token-block x head); drop redundant Q/K .contiguous() materialization in chunk_kda
hypothesis: q/k reach chunk_kda as narrow strided views from qkv.split (token stride = total_qkv_dim > H*D), so .contiguous() is a real gather-and-write pass that exists only to satisfy l2norm_fwd's x.view(). Consuming the strided view directly removes one write + one read per tensor for Q and K.
design: Additive strided kernel in l2norm.py with grid (cdiv(T,BT), H) and per-head base offset, two strides (x_stride_t, x_stride_h); rows within one program are tokens at a single uniform stride. Existing contiguous path left bit-for-bit unchanged as an early return; non-uniform layouts still fall back to .contiguous(). Then drop the two .contiguous() calls at kda.py:1225-1227.
design_correction_round_0: First sketch proposed a SINGLE runtime row stride over the flattened [T*H, D] view. That is wrong: flattened row (t,h) starts at t*tot + h*D, so one stride r would need r == D AND r == tot, i.e. tot == H*D, which is false since tot = q_dim+k_dim+v_dim. Corrected to the 2D-grid/two-stride form above, matching the addressing gdn_prefill_qkv_prepare_kernel (l2norm.py:122-216) already uses for strided [T,H,D] Q/K.
implementation_traps: Strided branch must allocate output via torch.empty(x.shape, ...), NOT torch.empty_like(x): preserve_format cannot be relied on to return a packed buffer for strided input, and the packed (H*D, 1) output block pointer depends on it.
Tighten the existing assert y.stride(-1) == 1 (l2norm.py:83) to assert output contiguity on the strided branch.
D=128 on the real shape stays in the D <= 512 branch (l2norm.py:92), so l2norm_fwd_kernel1 needs no change.
static_estimate: ~100 MB HBM traffic per layer per 8K prefill at H=12, D=128, bf16 (~25.2 MB/tensor); order ~12 us/layer at an assumed ~8 TB/s. ESTIMATE ONLY, NOT MEASURED.
selection_basis: static code reading, NOT a measured limiter
reason_not_promoted: Blocked before implementation: contract requires the 62-case correctness matrix + FP32 oracle + fixed-seed precision to pass on the exact base BEFORE editing (AC2), and requires the candidate to be selected from a MEASURED limiter (AC3/AC4). This host has no GB300 GPU (nvidia-smi/ncu/nsys/nvcc absent, macOS Darwin 25.2.0 arm64) and no bench harness (bench/correctness.py, bench/benchmark.py absent; workloads.resolved.json absent; k3ctl absent). Implementing now would invert the contract's required order and yield a diff that AC4/AC5 cannot certify.
must_confirm_before_implementing: Re-check against the AC3 NCU/NSYS baseline; drop C1 if the profile shows a different limiter.
Benchmark on the safe-gate configuration (lower_bound=-5.0 per checkpoint), not the default gate.
At the 8K serving shape fuse_diagonal/fuse_recompute are OFF (B*NT*H = 1536 > 256 heuristic in kda.py:1141-1148); profile that path, not the fused one.
invariants_reviewed: public chunk_kda ABI unchanged; l2norm_fwd gains no required parameter
output remains a fresh allocation (no in-place write to caller qkv)
v.contiguous() must NOT be removed: v is reused as the output buffer o in chunk_gla_fwd_o_gk (kda.py:1185)
non-uniformly-strided inputs fall back to .contiguous(), preserving current fallback layouts; contiguous path unchanged bit-for-bit

per-row fp32 reduction over BD=next_power_of_2(D)=128 is unchanged, and row-wise reduction is insensitive to which rows share a block, so numerics expected bitwise-identical (must be confirmed by the precision diagnostic, not assumed)

all other l2norm_fwd callers verified contiguous: kda_cutedsl.py:131-132 and ascend_kda_backend.py:48-49 call .contiguous() explicitly; chunk.py:111-112 is guarded by input_guard (fla/utils.py:145-158) one level up; l2norm.py:247,280 are already-packed branches
gate math, state-pool indexing, write-back and FP32 tracking untouched
notes: Not a copy of the accepted prefill-kda patch: that added gdn_prefill_qkv_prepare_fwd for the GDN FlashInfer path, which still materializes then norms in two passes. C1 removes the materialization on the KDA path instead. See .kda-task/docs/draft.md section 3.

title: Load h pre-transposed in chunk_gla_fwd_kernel_o instead of tl.trans per i_k iteration
hypothesis: kda.py:819-840 builds the h block pointer in (V,K) layout and transposes in-register every i_k iteration. A transposed block pointer ((K,V), (1,K), order (0,1)) loads [BK,BV] directly. Same idiom already used for k at kda.py:288-293.
payoff_uncertain: tl.trans on a register tile may compile to nothing more than a different MMA operand selection (worth 0%), or may force a shared-memory round-trip per iteration (worth something at BK x BV up to 64x128). On Blackwell/tcgen05 the operand-layout constraints decide it. Answerable ONLY from the NCU report: look for shared-memory traffic and instruction count inside this kernel.
selection_basis: static code reading, NOT a measured limiter
reason_not_promoted: Same blocker as c1 (no GB300, no bench harness on this host). Additionally: unlike c1, c2's payoff cannot even be estimated statically, so it must not be implemented before the NCU report settles whether the transpose costs anything.
implementation_traps: Keep the .to(b_qg.dtype) cast at kda.py:840: h = k.new_empty(...) (chunk_delta_h.py:396) inherits k's dtype -- bf16 on the real path so the cast is a no-op there, but fp32 if k ever is. Dropping it silently changes the dot's input precision.
The i_k >= 0 guard at kda.py:839 is always true (i_k is a loop index from 0) -- dead scaffolding, not logic. Do not mistake it for a condition to preserve.
allow_tf32=False on the second dot (kda.py:865) is a different dot on a different path; do not unify it as a drive-by.
notes: Fallback if the AC3 profile contradicts c1. See .kda-task/docs/draft.md section 3bis.

title: fp32 gate tensor g traffic (NOT worked up -- very likely out of contract bounds)
observation: kda_gate_chunk_cumsum allocates g as fp32 (kda.py:1061, output_dtype default torch.float). At T=8192, H=12, K=128 that is ~50 MB per layer, read by chunk_kda_fwd_intra, chunk_gated_delta_rule_fwd_h and chunk_gla_fwd_kernel_o -- several hundred MB of reads per layer, plausibly larger than c1's target.
reason_not_worked_up: g holds a log2-space cumulative sum consumed by exp2. Narrowing it is a PRECISION change to the gate, not a dataflow change, and the contract requires gate semantics preserved and FP32 tracking intact. Recorded so that a profile pointing at gate traffic is not mistaken for an unexplored opportunity: the reason it is unexplored is that it is very likely out of bounds, and confirming that needs the precision diagnostic rather than a benchmark.
selection_basis: static code reading; not a candidate

title: Increase chunk_size from 64 to 128
reason_not_promoted: 11 oracle cases failed on nonzero_state/permuted_slots; output relative RMS approximately 1.0. The 64-token state/chunk ABI cannot be changed this way.

title: Decrease chunk_size from 64 to 32
reason_not_promoted: Correctness produced non-finite outputs on nonzero_state, permuted_slots, strided_slots, padded_state_index and fp32_track cases.

title: H-stage tile BV 64
hypothesis: The NSYS kda_capture profile identified chunk_gated_delta_rule_fwd_kernel_h_blockdim64 as the dominant full-pipeline stage; doubling BV from 32 to 64 halves the V-grid programs.
reason_not_promoted: Full 51-case paired benchmark was below the 1.03x gate and long-prefill cases regressed about 8%; the larger tile increases register/occupancy pressure on the dominant shape.

title: H-stage 8 warps at BV 32
hypothesis: More warps may reduce the dominant H-stage dot/recurrent latency without increasing the BV tile.
reason_not_promoted: Full 51-case paired benchmark regressed 2.88%; the modest long-sequence improvement did not offset broad batched/short-shape regressions.

title: H-stage 2 warps at BV 32
hypothesis: Fewer warps may reduce register pressure while retaining the baseline BV tile.
reason_not_promoted: Full 51-case paired benchmark regressed 2.48%; no stable end-to-end gain.

title: H-stage BV 16 for occupancy relief
hypothesis: NCU showed 46 KB dynamic shared memory/block and only about three active blocks/SM; halving BV should reduce resource pressure and improve long-prefill occupancy.
reason_not_promoted: Long single/batched sequences improved, but the full 51-case geomean was 1.0180x, below the 1.03x gate; the result is not an accepted end-to-end optimization.

title: O-stage autotune key split by physical batch
reason_not_promoted: No reproducible 3% gain; the physical packed batch key was later shown to be constant at one.

title: O-stage physical-batch key with base configs only
reason_not_promoted: The isolated 1.1025x run did not reproduce; the independent final runs regressed.

title: O-stage autotune key split by logical scheduler batch
reason_not_promoted: The preliminary 1.0558x result failed the two final independent runs.

title: O-stage autotune key split by logical batch and NT
reason_not_promoted: Smoke-only probe regressed; no full acceptance run was justified.

title: Akk empty/lower-triangle mask shortcut
reason_not_promoted: No measured end-to-end gain; source restored.

title: Explicit H-stage BV dispatch: BV16 for average sequence length >=2048, BV32 otherwise
hypothesis: Avoid mutable-state autotune and use the measured BV16 long-sequence path only where it helps, while preserving BV32 for short/batched requests.
reason_not_promoted: The structural dispatch is correct and improves long-prefill shapes, but the full 51-case geomean remains below the 1.03x gate. No source change is retained.

title: O-stage transpose-free H block view
hypothesis: Present the physically [V,K] H state as a logical [K,V] tile so the O-stage MMA can consume it without tl.trans per K tile.
precision_status: passed with zero acceptance violations; candidate-vs-baseline max relative RMS 0
reason_not_promoted: The transpose-free view passed correctness and precision but the aggregate 51-case geomean was 0.9951x; five paired trials were unstable and the candidate regressed short/batched shapes. Source restored to base.

title: H/O fused recurrent loop for long single-sequence prefill
hypothesis: For batch-1 untracked long prefill, emit O from the H recurrence while b_h and v_new are resident, eliminating H and v_new global-memory round trips and the separate O launch.
dispatch: cu_seqlens batch-1, q.shape[1] >= 2048, output_intermediate_states=false, track_state=None; all other calls use the untouched fallback.
precision_status: passed; candidate-vs-baseline zero acceptance violations, max relative RMS 0.000679; candidate-vs-oracle max relative RMS 0.003374
reason_not_promoted: Correctness and precision passed, but fusing O into the per-V-tile H recurrence increased register/live-value pressure and duplicated O work across the H grid. The aggregate 51-case geomean was 0.9859247893x; long single-sequence rows regressed to 0.6849x at 4K, 0.5502x at 8K and 0.4664x at 16K. Source restored to base; no image or service integration.
debugging_note: An initial r2 run omitted scale in the fused state term and failed continuation correctness; r3 supplied scale_o=scale and passed the full correctness gate. R2 evidence is retained separately.
